findings.body:
Both admin handlers are registered as bare `http.HandlerFunc` values. The previous `middleware.RequireRole("admin")` wrapper is gone, so `GET /api/v2/admin/users` and `POST /api/v2/admin/roles` no longer require an admin role. Any caller who can reach the server can list users and mutate roles.

Apply the same middleware on the subrouter (it already returns `func(http.Handler) http.Handler`, which `mux.Router.Use` accepts):

```suggestion
	v2 := r.PathPrefix("/api/v2").Subrouter()
	v2.Use(middleware.RequireRole("admin"))
	v2.Handle("/admin/users", http.HandlerFunc(a.listUsers)).Methods("GET")
	v2.Handle("/admin/roles", http.HandlerFunc(a.editRoles)).Methods("POST")
```

summary:
I'd recommend not merging until admin authorization is restored on the new `/api/v2` routes.

The PathPrefix subrouter itself is a normal gorilla/mux grouping. The rewrite also dropped `middleware.RequireRole("admin")`, which previously wrapped both `listUsers` and `editRoles`. Those handlers now sit on `GET /api/v2/admin/users` and `POST /api/v2/admin/roles` with no role check in `routes()`. The natural cleanup is `v2.Use(middleware.RequireRole("admin"))` on the subrouter (same `func(http.Handler) http.Handler` shape as the old wrapper).

Callers of the previous `/admin/users` and `/admin/roles` paths will 404 after this move; that matches the stated versioning intent, so it is not filed as a defect. Confirm clients and any reverse-proxy rules are updated in the same rollout.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: Base wrapped both admin handlers with middleware.RequireRole("admin"); head registers bare HandlerFuncs on /api/v2/admin/* and RequireRole no longer appears anywhere, so admin authorization was dropped.
